title: SaiVLA-JEPA: Evaluating Future Latent Prediction in JEPA-Conditioned VLA Control
abstract: arXiv:2610.38508v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs) learn to predict representations rather than pixels, offering a compact way to model how visual scenes evolve. We ask whether this predictive objective improves closed-loop control when a vision-language-action (VLA) policy already uses V-JEPA features. We call our JEPA-conditioned flow policy family SaiVLA-JEPA. It combines a vision-language model with a diffusion transformer action expert and receives features from a frozen V-JEPA encoder. Two lightweight auxiliary heads predict future representations during training and are omitted at inference, leaving the action sampler unchanged. We compare policies without JEPA features, with current JEPA conditioning, and with additional future supervision on 10,030 paired LIBERO-Plus episodes. translated_title: SaiVLA-JEPA：在JEPA条件化的VLA控制中评估未来潜在预测
translated_abstract: 联合嵌入预测架构（JEPA）学习预测表征而非像素，为建模视觉场景如何演化提供了一种紧凑的方式。我们探究当视觉-语言-动作（VLA）策略已经使用V-JEPA特征时，这种预测目标是否仍能改善闭环控制。我们将这一JEPA条件化的流策略家族命名为SaiVLA-JEPA，它将视觉-语言模型与扩散变换器动作专家相结合，并接收来自冻结的V-JEPA编码器的特征。两个轻量级辅助头在训练期间预测未来表征，在推理时被省略，动作采样器保持不变。我们在10,030对LIBERO-Plus episode上比较了三种策略：不使用JEPA特征、使用当前JEPA条件化、以及附加未来监督。当前JEPA条件化达到约82.5%的成功率，而不使用JEPA时为71.6%，而未来监督在评估中未带来可检测的总体增益。
tldr: 该研究发现，在VLA机器人控制中，用当前V-JEPA特征进行条件化可显著提升成功率（82.5% vs 71.6%），但额外引入未来潜在表征预测的监督并未带来可检测的增益。
en_tdlr: Conditioning VLA policies on current V-JEPA features substantially improves control success (82.5% vs 71.6%), but additional future latent prediction supervision yields no detectable aggregate gain.
